source_profile.name: screen_document
source_profile.notes: Screen recordings, document and page content. TUNED @1: the declared default admission is localized block_max salience at 0.20 — the SAME cutoff physical_scene carries, never lowered — which clears on a screen change large enough to register on the 48x36 gate frame (a highlighted cell, a popup, a UI element). A fixed low-rate coast remains mandatory underneath it: a full-PAGE, text-scale edit still dilutes below every calibrated cutoff (see the measured evidence below), so the coast — not the tuned admission — is what keeps that harder residual case observed. A client whose content is dominated by page-scale edits should still register their own page-change / phash / OCR signal (register_detector) and A/B it with `percept eval` — see docs/how-to/tune-admission.md. An unreadable content key defaults to temporal-proximity unknown-continuity (SCREEN_UNKNOWN_CONTINUITY_GAP_S) rather than a fresh provisional subject per tick. Measured with percept-doctor on probes/01-screen-walkthrough/data/clean.mp4 (36s accounting screen recording, 180 frames, 1920x1080, containing a hard cut between two different documents): mean max 0.0163 vs threshold 0.100 -> 0 admitted; block_max max 0.0919 vs threshold 0.200 -> 0 admitted; p95 max 0.0743 vs threshold 0.150 -> 0 admitted. block_max amplifies the localized signal 5.6x over the mean as designed and still lands under HALF its own cutoff. Cause: the tier-0 gate frame is 48x36 greyscale (runtime/source.py) and block_max reads an 8x6 grid over it, so one block is ~6x6 px of a downsampled 1080p screen — a document-sized edit is diluted away. This is an under-resolved EYE, not a mis-selected statistic, and it is NOT fixed by lowering a threshold (the same cutoffs carry physical-scene precision).

ladder.winner_rule: the earliest rung, in the operator's declared order, that meets EVERY supplied bar
